items.title: PTI slams govt for ‘flouting’ SC order, opp says it will approach SC over contempt
items.description: ISLAMABAD: The PTI on Friday accused the government of committing contempt of court by “flouting” the Supreme Court’s order to shift incarcerated party founder Imran Khan to Shifa International Hospital, and announced that it would approach the apex court on Saturday. On Tuesday, the SC had directed the government to move Imran to Shifa International Hospital, a private facility. All eyes were on the hospital with a heavy police presence stationed on Thursday night. However, Information Minister Attaullah Tarar revealed on Friday that Imran was instead taken to the government-run Pakistan Institute of Medical Sciences (Pims). It is worth mentioning that the SC had ordered that Imran’s medical reports or information concerning his health should not be used for political purposes. On Friday, Imran’s sister Uzma Khan, who was present for his medical examination, addressed a press conference in Islamabad alongside his personal physician, Dr Faisal Sultan. She said they had received a phone call on Thursday to reach Adiala jail, where Imran is incarcerated. “So we reached the Adiala jail at around 8-8:30pm,” she added. Uzma said they were then taken to a deputy superintendent of police’s room, whom she identified as Sibtain. “Later, Sibtain sahib asked Dr Sultan to go outside the room with him and me to stay in the room. Then, after around 10 to 15 minutes, a female assistant sub-inspector took me to a car.” She added that all this while, police did not answer any of her queries, including those about Dr Sultan. Uzma said she was then taken to Pims. “I asked them why you have brought me here; the SC has instructed for (Imran’s) treatment at Shifa International Hospital. At that, they told me we were there for a follow-up regarding Imran’s eye.” Imran has been taken to Pims for treatment multiple times after his eye ailment — right central retinal vein occlusion (CRVO) — came to light in late January. Recounting her visit to Pims on Thursday night, Uzma said, “There was darkness all around.” She said she was taken to an office as a man used the torch from his mobile phone to light the way. She said she assumed the office belonged to the head of a department at Pims. “We sat there for a while, and then they took me upstairs. When I went upstairs, Imran was sitting there. He too was a little surprised. He then stood up, he was in shock. He told the doctors who were with him that she is my sister and we were meeting after 10 months,” she recalled. Uzma said she told him he was there for a checkup and would later be taken to Shifa International Hospital, adding that she also enquired about Dr Sultan at Pims but received no response. She said they were then taken back to an office, where an examination of Imran’s eye was conducted. “There were two to three doctors there, but I was not familiar with any of them. They introduced me to Dr Arif, but I did not know any of the others,” she said. She said they were then taken to an office where an examination of Imran’s eye was conducted. “They asked, ‘Khan sahib , which eye drops do you use?’ “I said if the drops they had prescribed were not mentioned in their notes. None of them knew,” she added. One of the doctors said Imran needed to immediately undergo a test as his blood vessel had to be checked, she recalled, adding that she told the doctors they would be going to Shifa International Hospital for an examination and checkup. Uzma said they were again shifted to another place after that, where the doctors said Imran had to be administered an injection. They also did other tests and said the eye condition and haemorrhage situation had improved, she said. Then, a doctor came and checked Imran’s blood pressure, which was 120/80 or 70, she said. “He (Imran) asked me what was happening, and I told him he would be taken to Shifa International Hospital for complete examination and, if required, any treatment. He was happy with that,” she recalled. All this while, Uzma said, Imran kept telling her just one thing: that he had been subjected to “cruelty”. “He said they were torturing them. He said a doctor who had visited him had concluded that his health deteriorated due to not having any human contact. “He said he was not provided any reading material or television for the past 10 months,” she said. Uzma added that Imran also said when he would complain about his health to prison doctors, “no one would listen or care”. She further quoted him as telling her that a doctor who examined him on August 10 said that he had severe anxiety due to “mental torture in solitary confinement”, and that anxiety caused high blood pressure. Uzma said that, complaining of his health condition, Imran said Egyptian president Mohamed Morsi “was killed the same way, by giving him stress and keeping him in solitary confinement”. “He also said that Bushra Bibi was also being kept in solitary confinement […] He kept saying that they were subjecting him to cruelty,” Uzma said, adding that Imran told her that he was given newspapers and television for two days, after which these facilities were taken back. She also rejected reports that Imran was not happy about being taken to Shifa International Hospital. Continuing her account, Uzma said they were taken to the Adiala jail instead of Shifa International Hospital from Pims. “When I disembarked the car I was in, I saw Dr Sultan getting off another car,” she said, adding that Imran’s message for Khyber Pakhtunkhwa Sohail Afridi was to expedite and intensify his movement. Speaking after her, Dr Sultan said he was taken to Shifa International Hospital from the Adiala jail while Uzma was taken to Pims. “There were security arrangements there, and I was asked to wait at the hospital. We kept waiting for around two to two and a half hours. I kept asking and they kept on saying that he (Imran) was arriving. I think they, too, were not completely aware of what the plan exactly was. “Around 4:15-30pm, they told me that it seemed he (Imran) may not be able to come, and he probably had returned, and that I too should return,” he said. Dr Sultan said he saw Uzma disembarking from another car upon reaching the Adiala jail, and then the two came to know that they were taken to separate hospitals. Replying to a question, Uzma said Imran was not aware of the situation outside as he did not have access to newspapers and television. To a query about Imran’s health, she said he was “fit”, his blood pressure was normal and vision had improved. “Just a small haemorrhage is left,” she added. KP CM Afridi also spoke at the press conference, expressing regret over the government and administration’s conduct on Thursday. “A decision by three judges of the Supreme Court was thrown in the dustbin,” he said, terming the act contempt of court. “Judges across Pakistan now have to decide whether to get their decisions implemented or shut courts,” he remarked. As Uzma conveyed Imran’s message to him, he said he would be expediting his movement for Imran’s release. Moreover, he said, the PTI would file a contempt plea over Thursday night’s episode. The KP CM also rejected claims that any PTI workers had gathered outside Shifa International Hospital on Thursday night. Opposition to approach SC on Saturday The opposition’s joint parliamentary party on Friday said the government had committed contempt of court by failing to implement the SC’s order to shift incarcerated PTI founder Imran Khan to Shifa International Hospital, and announced that it would approach the apex court on Saturday. According to a statement released by opposition alliance Tehreek Tahafuz Ayeen-i-Pakistan (TTAP), the opposition’s joint parliamentary party held a meeting at Parliament House, chaired by National Assembly Opposition Leader Mehmood Khan Achakzai and attended by Senate Opposition Leader Allama Raja Nasir Abbas, PTI Chairman Barrister Gohar Khan, PTI Secretary General Salman Akram Raja, Khyber Pakhtunkhwa Chief Minister Sohail Afridi and other leaders. The meeting discussed the country’s overall political situation, the health of the PTI founder, the implementation of the apex court’s orders, parliamentary affairs and the opposition’s future political and public strategy, the statement said. During the meeting, serious concern was expressed over the non-implementation of the SC’s orders to shift Imran to Shifa International Hospital, and it was decided to adopt a “constitutional and legal course of action”, it added. “The joint parliamentary party members stated that by failing to execute the Supreme Court’s verdict, the government has committed contempt of court,” the statement said, adding, “Consequently, it was decided to approach the Supreme Court tomorrow.” The meeting participants expressed “deep concern” over the health of Imran. The members “categorically stated that no compromise would be accepted regarding his health and medical treatment, noting that the government had staged a drama concerning his well-being,” the statement claimed. Regarding the September 27 long march, the meeting announced its decision to uphold the PTI’s plan for a full-scale protest on the announced date, it stated. “Detailed consultations were held regarding the September 27 protest and long march, with a decision to invite all opposition parties to participate.” According to the statement, the meeting agreed to intensify the public contact campaign across the country, including Punjab, and make political activities more organised and effective. “The joint parliamentary party expressed its firm resolve to continue a united struggle for the protection of the Constitution, democracy, the rule of law and parliamentary principles. “It was decided that the opposition parties would make all future key political and parliamentary decisions through mutual consultation, unity and solidarity,” the statement said. The TTAP statement added that the meeting participants fully endorsed the establishment of the grand opposition alliance, agreeing to make the coalition more “active, organised and effective”. It also welcomed the inclusion of JUI-F chief Maulana Fazlur Rehman and other opposition parties in the grand opposition alliance, stating that a broader alliance would further strengthen and amplify the opposition’s voice, both in parliament and among the public. “Detailed consultations were held on the opposition alliance’s future political, parliamentary and public strategy, with an agreement to further accelerate mutual coordination and consultation in this regard,” the statement concluded. ‘Theatrics and misleading conduct’ Separately, PTI Central Information Secretary Sheikh Waqas Akram also criticised the government for what he described as an “attempt to conceal its non-compliance with the Supreme Court’s order”. Referring to Tarar’s X posts, he said they had once again “exposed the government’s familiar pattern of theatrics and misleading conduct”. “The Supreme Court’s order has not been implemented and only a superficial exercise had been carried out to mislead the court and the nation,” Akram said in a statement. He added that “declaring the PTI founder medically fit after a few hours of what appears to have been a merely symbolic exercise and then shifting him back to the Adiala jail before dawn raises serious questions”. Moreover, “blaming PTI workers with false allegations to conceal the violation of a court order is not a new tactic but an old pattern of government theatrics and deception”, he said, adding that PTI workers had not gathered at Shifa International Hospital, nor had they created any security concerns. “There are no media reports of any security situation,” he stated. “Conducting a secret transfer in the middle of the night and then blaming PTI workers for compromising security exposes the contradictions and falsehoods in the government’s own narrative.” He demanded that the government make Imran’s complete medical reports public and implement the Supreme Court’s order in letter and spirit. “Imran Khan’s health is not a matter of political propaganda; it is a fundamental human right. Instead of engaging in political theatrics, the government must ensure full compliance with the directions of the SC,” he asserted. “Things are not as simple as Attaullah Tarar is attempting to portray them,” he continued, adding that mere statements and symbolic measures were not sufficient. “The government must ensure transparency in the matter of Imran Khan’s health and provide him with the required medical facilities and an independent medical examination, as directed by the court.”

items.title: New Dansoman drainage to measure 2 metres high and 5 metres wide – Engineer Tsegah
items.description: The new underground drainage system being constructed at Dansoman Junction, popularly known as Hansonic, will measure two metres in height and five metres in width, according to the Maintenance Engineer for the Ablekuma North Municipality, Kwaku Tsegah. Mr Tsegah explained that the new drain would be constructed underground, with the surface above it serving as a roadway. According to him, the new structure would be significantly larger than the existing drain, which he said had outlived its purpose and was no longer adequate to handle the volume of water in the area. The project is being undertaken by the Department of Urban Roads as part of efforts to address persistent flooding and drainage challenges at the busy Dansoman Junction. Mr Tsegah said the first phase of the project is focused on stopping and diverting running water into the old drainage system. He explained that this would enable engineers to safely undertake the construction of the new underground drain. The new drainage system is expected to improve stormwater flow and provide a lasting solution to the flooding that has affected the area for several years. The project is also expected to improve access and road conditions around the busy junction once construction is completed.

items.title: Kozah/faciliter les échanges commerciaux : Des parlementaires et acteurs économiques du septentrion outillé
items.description: Kara, 21 août (ATOP) – Un atelier national de sensibilisation sur le Guichet unique du commerce extérieur (GUCE), la Zone de libre-échange continentale africaine (ZLECAf), ainsi que sur la Solution automatisé de marquage (SAM) et le commerce électronique s’est tenu les 20 et 21 août à Kara. L’atelier est organisé par le ministère délégué chargé du Commerce et du Contrôle de la Qualité, et s’inscrit dans la politique globale de modernisation des procédures commerciales et de promotion des échanges. Il a réuni une centaine d’acteurs économiques et élus des régions des Savanes, de la Kara et de la Centrale Un pan des participants en salle La rencontre vise à résorber le déficit d’information des acteurs locaux pour leur permettre de tirer pleinement profit des réformes économiques engagées par le gouvernement. Il s’agit de renforcer les capacités des participants sur les mécanismes de facilitation du commerce. La formation entend vulgariser le fonctionnement du GUCE, sensibiliser aux opportunités du marché continental, clarifier les obligations liées au SAM et promouvoir l’usage des outils numériques de commercialisation comme la plateforme Togo Trade Portal. Les travaux se sont déroulés en exposés interactifs, démonstrations pratiques et en échanges d’expériences. Ils ont permis aux acteurs mobilisés d’être outillés sur les avantages du GUCE, les opportunités offertes par la ZLECAf, les objectifs et obligations de la SAM, ainsi que le commerce électronique comme levier de compétitivité. Le préfet de la Kozah, Col. Bonfoh Faré, a au nom du gouverneur de la région Kara, exhorté les participants à s’approprier ces outils technologiques, afin d’impulser le développement économique régional. Le secrétaire général du ministère délégué chargé du Commerce et du Contrôle de la Qualité, Comlan Yakpey, a expliqué que, l’implication ciblée des parlementaires et élus consulaires découle de leur proximité directe avec les populations et de leur rôle de relais d’informations. Pour le directeur général de SICPA Togo, Tchamdja Sosso, expert-formateur, la SAM constitue un levier de traçabilité indispensable pour sécuriser les marchandises, protéger les consommateurs, lutter contre la contrefaçon et le commerce illicite. L’élaboration d’un rapport général assorti de recommandations a marqué la fin de cette formation. ATOP/AE/TAL/AR

items.title: Victims of terrorism
items.description: OVER the past quarter century, Pakistan has paid a staggering toll in lives lost to terrorism . Therefore, today, as the world observes the International Day of Remembrance of and Tribute to the Victims of Terrorism, the state must pledge to root out the scourge of violent extremism, and continue to care for the families of the victims. From 2001, when America’s so-called war on terror began, till 2022, terrorism in Pakistan claimed at least 83,000 lives. From 2022 till the present, several thousand lives have been added to this grim tally, due to the ongoing terrorist activities in the country, which picked up pace after the Afghan Taliban’s takeover of Kabul in 2021. Cumulatively, over the course of these 25 years, terrorists have struck mosques and churches, bazaars and processions, schools and madressahs. It took several military operations to quell the post-2001 wave of terrorism, especially as terrorist attacks increased in frequency from 2007 onwards. Today, we find ourselves back to square one, as a new generation of terrorists wreaks havoc across the land. Much has been written about counterterrorism strategies; but keeping with the theme of the day — ‘Healing through Memory’ — we must never forget those who were martyred or injured in acts of terrorism. One way of doing so would be for the state to ensure that the next of kin of victims of terrorism, whether security personnel or civilians, are looked after financially. The state does announce Shuhada packages , and it should be ensured that assistance is offered in a transparent and dignified manner. Victims who are injured, or left permanently disabled and thus unable to work, need to be looked after. Apart from the financial aspect, victims of terrorism and their families need to be offered professional psychological support to expedite mental recovery. Above all else, to honour the memory of victims, the state must vow to permanently uproot the menace of terrorism from Pakistan. Published in Dawn, August 21st, 2026

FIFA, UEFA ban 6 countries from facing each other
items.description: Football is often seen as a game that brings countries together, but political disputes and conflicts have sometimes made certain international fixtures too sensitive to stage. In some cases, FIFA and UEFA have kept national teams apart because of political tensions, territorial disputes or security concerns. Here are six notable pairings that have been kept apart. Spain vs Gibraltar Spain and Gibraltar have a long-running dispute over sovereignty. Gibraltar has been under British control since 1713, but Spain continues to claim the territory. The political disagreement has also affected football, with UEFA keeping the two sides apart in competition draws because of the sensitive nature of the dispute. Armenia vs Azerbaijan Armenia and Azerbaijan have been kept apart because of their long-running conflict over Nagorno-Karabakh. The dispute has led to several periods of armed conflict, most recently in 2020 and 2023. UEFA has also prevented clubs from the two countries from being drawn against each other in European competitions. The tensions have affected players too. Armenian international Henrikh Mkhitaryan missed Arsenal’s 2019 Europa League final in Baku because of security concerns. Kosovo vs Serbia Kosovo declared independence from Serbia in 2008, but Serbia does not recognise it and continues to claim the territory. The dispute has extended to football, with UEFA preventing Kosovo and Serbia from being drawn against each other in its competitions. Kosovo vs Bosnia and Herzegovina Bosnia and Herzegovina is another country that does not recognise Kosovo’s independence. Political divisions within Bosnia, particularly the position of Republika Srpska, have contributed to the country’s stance. UEFA has consequently kept the two national teams apart. Kosovo vs Russia Russia also does not recognise Kosovo’s independence and continues to support Serbia’s position on the territory. The two countries have therefore been kept apart in UEFA competitions. Russia’s subsequent suspension from international football has further prevented the fixture from taking place. Russia vs Ukraine The ongoing war between Russia and Ukraine has also made a meeting between the two national teams impossible. Following Russia’s invasion of Ukraine in 2022, FIFA and UEFA suspended Russian national teams and clubs from their competitions. The conflict has also severely disrupted Ukrainian football, with clubs forced to relocate matches and players affected by the war. items.title: Iran president says time to end war while in position of strength
items.description: Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian said Friday it was time to end the months-long Middle East war with the United States because Tehran was in a position of strength over Washington. “It is better that we bring the war to an end now as we are in a position of power and dignity, and the whole world acknowledges our victory and emphasises that America has attacked our schools, hospitals and infrastructure in violation of all regulations and is hated around the world,” he said in a meeting with doctors. His comments came after Iran’s foreign ministry accused the US of “economic terrorism” and “crimes against humanity” after Washington said it would ramp up sanctions to heap pressure on Tehran. “The perpetrators and instigators of these sanctions are deserving of trial and punishment for committing such heinous crimes,” it said in a statement carried by state media. US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent on Thursday vowed Washington would “collapse” the Iranian regime with its threatened campaign nearly six months since their war began. China also criticised the move, saying that US “sanctions and pressure” would not resolve the Middle East conflict. Washington had urged other governments including Beijing to join efforts to isolate the Iranian economy. Asked about US President Donald Trump’s threats, Chinese foreign ministry spokesman Lin Jian told reporters on Friday that “sanctions and pressure will not help resolve the issue”. “China calls on all relevant parties to take responsible measures and resolve the problem through political and diplomatic means,” he said. items.title: Interior Minister orders Police to crack down on vigilante groups, unauthorised security forces
items.description: The Minister for the Interior, Muntaka Mubarak, has directed the Ghana Police Service to intensify efforts to dismantle vigilante groups and prevent individuals and organisations from forming unauthorised forces for self-protection. He warned that the growing practice of political parties, chiefs, individuals and other groups establishing their own security forces posed a threat to national peace and security and must not be allowed to take root. Mr Muntaka issued the directive at the opening of a regional commanders’ conference at the Police Headquarters in Accra, where he urged senior officers to remain vigilant and take decisive action against activities capable of undermining public order. “We observe with concern a new trend of chiefs, political parties, individuals, and some organisations building forces for self-protection. The Vigilantism and Related Offences Act 2019, Act 999, is clear on this matter,” he said. The Minister stressed that only security forces authorised by the state had the mandate to provide protection, and charged police commanders to identify and deal with individuals and groups operating outside the law. “These are illegal and should not be tolerated. There should be no forces for protection of any person or group except those authorised by the state. I therefore charge you and your commanders to nip this in the bud and bring perpetrators to book,” he said. Mr Muntaka also ordered an immediate halt to the recording and circulation of videos and other content showing recruits undergoing training at security service institutions. He expressed concern about officers and trainers allowing unauthorised recordings from training schools to be shared on social media, warning that the practice could undermine the integrity and security of the institutions. “I therefore direct all service commanders to ensure that appropriate controls are put in place to prevent the unauthorised recording, publication and circulation of images or videos of recruits in training,” he stated.

items.title: Nasarawa 2027: Adamu’s campaign rejects claim ex-IGP lacks platform
items.description: The campaign organisation of former Inspector-General of Police, Mohammed Abubakar Adamu, has rejected claims that the former police chief lacks a political platform to contest the 2027 Nasarawa State governorship election. The organisation was reacting to comments by the Nasarawa State Chairman of the All Progressives Congress (APC), Dr Aliyu Bello, who reportedly questioned Adamu’s platform for the contest. In a statement on Friday signed by its Director of Media and Strategic Communications, Otaru Douglas, the campaign described Bello’s position as “false, laughable and born out of panic.” It maintained that Adamu remained in the governorship race and had secured a platform through his membership of the Social Democratic Party (SDP). According to the campaign, Adamu’s departure from the APC followed what it described as a controversial governorship primary and was intended to provide an alternative political platform for voters in the state. “Adamu’s defection from the APC, following the charade called a primary election, was a strategic move to a credible and people-oriented platform — the Social Democratic Party (SDP),” the statement said. The organisation expressed confidence that Adamu would secure victory in the 2027 election, citing what it described as his growing support among voters across the state. “The IGP is contesting the 2027 governorship election and, by the grace of God and the will of the people of Nasarawa State, he will win convincingly,” it said. The campaign also took aim at Bello’s stewardship of the APC in Nasarawa, particularly the party’s governorship primary. It alleged that the exercise had generated widespread criticism among APC members and stakeholders across the state’s 13 local government areas. “The governorship primary he superintended as State Chairman has been widely condemned by party members and stakeholders across the 13 LGAs as lacking transparency, fairness, and internal democracy,” the statement alleged. The organisation accused the APC chairman of resorting to personal attacks against Adamu and warned against further criticism of the former police chief. “We are therefore calling on Dr Aliyu Bello to stay in his political lane and face his party’s dwindling fortunes,” Douglas said. The campaign said Adamu’s political agenda remained centred on transparent governance, improved security and development, adding that his decision to contest under the SDP would not be affected by criticism from political opponents. It further declared that “no amount of intimidation and media blackmail” would alter what it described as the resolve of Nasarawa voters ahead of the election. The organisation also warned that any further attempt to “disparage, defame, or malign” Adamu would attract what it described as a “firm, proportionate, and decisive political response.” The post Nasarawa 2027: Adamu’s campaign rejects claim ex-IGP lacks platform appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Liberal Families Are Looking Pretty Traditional
items.description: Picture an old-fashioned, idealized American scene. Young kids walk to and from a redbrick public schoolhouse; almost every kid’s commute is less than 10 minutes. On warm weekend days, the children run lemonade stands, doing brisk business. Their parents host a Christmas-tree-and-baked-goods sale on the school field every December, which draws a boisterous crowd. And about those parents: They’re almost all married. Divorce and single parenthood are rare. The whole tableau is, at first glance, a social conservative’s dream come true. This scene exists in the real world. The neighborhood is my own; the elementary school is my kids’ school. But this is no conservative small town. It’s an urban neighborhood in Washington, D.C., a city where Kamala Harris beat Donald Trump 90 percent to 6 percent in the most recent election. Virtually all of the parents in this neighborhood are highly educated Democrats. Judging from what I see in my community here, these deep-blue Washington families are the kinds of families that so many conservatives value. The strong marriages of elite blue America—families whose lives are, in a way, pretty darn conservative—offer a useful counterpoint to the simplistic culture-war narrative. Elite blue Americans are an attractive boogeyman for pundits on the right, who regularly write articles about how such people are pushing outré sexual and family values. But when you actually look at these people, you see a lot of folks who get married, have kids, stay married, and live lives that almost seem ripped from a Norman Rockwell painting. As the cultural commentator Aaron Renn put it , “If you want to see conservative values in practice, you’ll often find them among people who vote Democrat and align on the cultural left.” Conservatives might benefit from closely observing what’s going on here—liberal Americans achieving what seems to be the conservative goal of stable families. Some social scientists have, in fact, argued that blue values such as egalitarianism and secularism tend to produce stronger marriages than red values such as religiosity and traditional gender roles. A few data points support their thesis. For example, highly educated Americans are trending blue in their politics, and highly educated Americans are also more likely to be married. As couples move up the educational ladder from high-school degree to associate’s degree to bachelor’s degree to master’s degree, the marriage rate keeps climbing. [ From the July 2026 issue: How to save marriage ] But other data paint a different picture. Liberals and Democrats lag behind conservatives and Republicans in marrying and having children , and the gap is growing. As of 2024, among adults aged 30 to 50, Republicans are 18 points more likely than Democrats to be married, and Republican women aged 25 to 35 are 31 points more likely to be mothers. Although delayed marriage and childbearing by Democrats is part of the story, some of the gap is undoubtedly Democrats opting out of marriage and parenthood altogether. Blue values alone don’t seem to directly produce stable families. I’d offer this hypothesis instead: At least among many highly educated Democrats, stable families display a mixture of blue and red traits. That’s what you see in my neighborhood, as I recently wrote about for the Institute for Family Studies. On the blue, egalitarian side, almost every family has two working parents. Stay-at-home moms are scarce. Educational attainment tends to be pretty equal between spouses. And some of the more symbolic lifestyle markers also trend egalitarian. For example, based on the parent lists for my kids’ classrooms, only nine kids out of 50 (18 percent) have two parents who share a last name. But these families also display some more stereotypically red traits—including income hypergamy, meaning that fathers outearn mothers. In terms of income, there are three main career tiers among these well-educated D.C. parents. At the top of the income scale are the private-sector for-profit workers. In the middle are the government bureaucrats. And at the bottom are the nonprofit NGO workers. Most fathers are in the top or middle tier, while most mothers are in the middle or bottom one. (The small number of families with same-sex parents obviously don’t show this gendered division of income, but they also have two married parents who both work.) [ Read: The return of the Democratic manly man ] Why do these couples gravitate toward this gendered income division? Every couple is different, but for many families, this arrangement allows women to pursue career goals beyond remuneration. For example, one of my female colleagues (married, two young kids, separate last names) is working her self-described “dream job” prosecuting international money launderers in federal court. Her husband is a law-firm partner who makes most of the family’s income. My own household is similar: My wife has her dream job as an immunologist at the National Institutes of Health. It’s a career path that required several years as a poorly paid postdoc, during which I far outearned her. In Jane Austen novels, financially advantageous marriages helped women secure their social station. But in educated blue America, such marriages help women pursue their career goals—while maintaining a household income that can cover the cost of raising kids. Many of these families also have other traditionalist or red-coded markers. For example, many are surprisingly religious. I’d estimate that almost a third of my kids’ friends go to church on a weekly basis, mostly in mainline Protestant or Catholic denominations. This might not reach the churchgoing levels of devout Bible Belt communities, and the mix of churches is definitely different, with evangelical options notably few. But these elite liberals go to church at a higher rate than Americans as a whole . Elite liberals should be proud of their families—and they should preach what they practice. The conservative family scholar Brad Wilcox wasn’t wrong when he called it “hypocrisy” for liberals to publicly promote freewheeling family diversity even while they themselves follow traditional family patterns. Fortunately, some liberals are starting to speak up for the traditional family values generally out of fashion among liberals. In the past few years, for example, liberal writers such as Nicholas Kristof and center-left scholars such as Melissa Kearney have written about how a stable marriage is the best foundation for raising kids. The preaching, in other words, may be catching up to the practice. Let’s hope more people hear it.

items.title: Kozah / Entrepreneuriat et innovation : Sept porteurs de projets retenus pour un accompagnement à Kara
items.description: Kara, 21 août (ATOP) – Sept jeunes porteurs de projets entrepreneuriaux ont été retenus, le jeudi 20 août à Kara, pour bénéficier d’un accompagnement technique de six mois, à l’issue de l’initiative « Entrepreneurs Connect – Etape Kara », consacrée à la promotion de l’entrepreneuriat et de l’innovation. Placée sous le thème « Connecter les projets aux opportunités pour renforcer l’économie locale », la rencontre a réuni des porteurs de projets, des institutions financières et plusieurs acteurs de l’écosystème entrepreneurial de la région de la Kara. Sur les 30 participants à cette rencontre, 21 porteurs de projets ont présenté et défendu leurs initiatives devant un jury de trois membres. A l’issue de cette évaluation, sept projets ont été sélectionnés pour bénéficier d’un accompagnement technique pendant six mois Les cinq premiers lauréats ont été distingués par la remise de trophées. Kalaba Pyalo Prénam s’est classée première avec une note de 83,7 points sur 100. Le premier prix décerné à Kalaba Pyalo Prénam L’étape de Kara est la première d’une tournée qui devrait couvrir l’ensemble des régions du Togo. Cette foire aux projets est à l’actif de l’association Africa Coworkers, en partenariat avec le Centre d’accompagnement à la valorisation des résultats de la recherche-innovation dans le domaine des sciences et technologies (CAVRIS), le Réseau des jeunes producteurs et professionnels agricoles du Togo (REJEPPAT), le programme Formation en développement d’affaires (FoDA) et l’Université de Kara. Elle a bénéficié de l’appui technique et financier de la Coopération allemande, mise en œuvre par la GIZ à travers le programme de promotion de l’emploi pour les femmes et les groupes vulnérables au Togo (Emploi+). L’initiative s’inscrit dans la dynamique des actions engagées en faveur de l’entrepreneuriat, de l’innovation et de la mise en réseau des acteurs de l’écosystème entrepreneurial. L’objectif est de créer un cadre de rencontres et de collaboration entre les porteurs de projets et les différents acteurs de l’écosystème entrepreneurial. Il s’agit notamment de faciliter l’accès à l’accompagnement, aux opportunités stratégiques et aux ressources nécessaires au développement durable des initiatives entrepreneuriales. Les échanges ont permis aux jeunes de mieux connaître les opportunités disponibles dans la région et de s’imprégner des réalités liées à la mise en œuvre de leurs projets. Les participants ont également reçu des conseils et des orientations sur les mécanismes d’accompagnement et de financement. Des présentations ont notamment porté sur les structures et initiatives d’appui technique et financier notamment Widu, spécialisée dans l’octroi de subventions, ainsi que « Mercredi de l’entrepreneur » de l’Agence nationale de promotion et de garantie de financement des PME/PMI (ANPGE), organisée une fois par mois. Selon les organisateurs, la tenue de cette foire répond au besoin de mieux valoriser le potentiel entrepreneurial de la région de la Kara, qui dispose de nombreuses ressources encore insuffisamment exploitées, notamment en raison du déficit d’information, d’orientation et d’encadrement des jeunes. Les bénéficiaires, par la voix de leur porte-parole, Kalaba Pyalo Prénam, se sont engagés à mettre à profit les acquis de la rencontre et ont invité les autres porteurs de projets à se faire identifier, à saisir les opportunités disponibles et à croire en leurs capacités. ATOP/LER/TAL/AO

items.title: Young Ghanaians need markets and opportunities to turn skills into Jobs – Youth Advocates.
items.description: Young Ghanaians need greater access to markets, leadership opportunities and meaningful platforms to apply their skills if the country is to unlock the full potential of its youthful population, two youth development advocates have said. Co-founder and Chief Executive Officer of Ghana Fertilizer Limited, Nana Kusi Appiah, and founder of Youth in Transformative Development Africa (YIDA), Christabel Odonkor, say young people across different backgrounds share a common aspiration – to be given the opportunity to contribute, grow their businesses and create jobs. Their comments come as Ghana joins the global community to mark International Youth Day 2026, which is being observed on August 12 under the theme, “Different Contexts, Common Aspirations.” The theme recognises that although young people come from different backgrounds, communities and circumstances, they share common aspirations for quality education, meaningful work, entrepreneurship and opportunities to build better futures. The focus is particularly relevant to Ghana as the country continues to grapple with the challenge of translating the growing number of young people entering the labour market into productive employment and sustainable livelihoods. The Mastercard Foundation’s Africa Youth Employment Outlook 2026 highlights major transitions shaping the future of work, including the shift from agriculture to services, the movement of young people from rural to urban economies and the growing importance of relevant skills. The report also underscores the need for quality job creation, greater inclusion and stronger pathways to sustainable livelihoods. For Nana Kusi Appiah, who is a participant of the Kosmos Innovation Center programme, access to finance and business development support helped him transform an idea into a business producing fertilizer from organic waste for smallholder farmers in Ghana. He, however, believes access to finance must be matched with access to markets if young businesses are to survive, expand and create jobs. “First and foremost, I’ll speak about access to market because we believe the young people have been given the chance, right? We have to be given the opportunity to serve in those markets as well,” he said. According to Mr Appiah, young businesses often struggle to compete for contracts and tender opportunities because larger and more established companies tend to dominate procurement processes. “When it comes to tender opportunities, most of these winning the tenders are big businesses,” he noted. He is therefore calling for measures that would give qualified youth-led businesses a fair opportunity to participate in public and private procurement. “I believe if there is a quota given to young businesses to go out there and tender, we’ll also be able to do more and create more jobs,” he said. Mr Appiah stressed that providing funding without creating access to customers and markets could limit the impact of programmes designed to support young entrepreneurs. “Because without these good regulations, good opportunities out there for young businesses, we will access the funds, but then we won’t be able to grow and create more jobs,” he added. He said his own experience demonstrates how targeted support can help young entrepreneurs move from an idea to a viable business. According to him, the Kosmos Innovation Center programme, which partners with the Mastercard Foundation, provided business development support and skills that improved his confidence when engaging investors and other stakeholders. He said the support has enabled Ghana Fertilizer Limited to grow, contribute to job creation and support farmers through locally produced fertilizer. Beyond entrepreneurship, Mr Appiah believes Ghana must also prepare for a changing labour market, particularly as agriculture gradually gives way to services and other emerging sectors as major sources of employment for young people. “Years back, I mean most of agriculture used to employ the highest population of young people all over Ghana. But then currently this sector is gradually dropping. It’s pushing away from that and it’s employing more of the skills and also the services sectors as well,” he said. He believes greater investment in emerging sectors, coupled with stronger support for young entrepreneurs, could help expand employment opportunities and reduce the barriers facing young people entering the labour market. For Christabel Odonkor, however, the challenge goes beyond acquiring skills. She believes young people must also be provided with platforms to apply those skills, demonstrate their capabilities and contribute meaningfully to national development. “One of my greatest challenges was having the potential, but opportunity to utilize the skills that I have, and also to grow and then to meaningfully contribute to development,” she said. Ms Odonkor, a communication and development professional, public speaker, event host and women and youth advocate, said programmes such as Emerging Public Leaders of Ghana and YALI provided her with opportunities to develop her leadership capacity. Through the Emerging Public Leaders of Ghana programme, which is funded by the Mastercard Foundation, she said she gained valuable experience in leadership, collaboration, resilience and initiative-taking. She believes such interventions are increasingly important because the world of work is changing rapidly and traditional pathways can no longer adequately prepare young people for emerging opportunities. “We need a lot of reforms. The world is evolving, but then gone are the days that the traditional pathways that we had for young people were one-sided,” she said. Ms Odonkor is therefore calling for stronger collaboration between the education sector, government, development organisations and other institutions working on youth development. “We need a lot of reforms,” she stressed, arguing that young people need systems that effectively connect education and skills development to real opportunities. The Africa Youth Employment Outlook 2026 similarly points to the importance of ensuring that young people are equipped with relevant skills while creating stronger pathways into employment and entrepreneurship. The outlook highlights the changing nature of work across Africa, with young people increasingly moving beyond traditional agricultural livelihoods into services and other emerging sectors. Against this backdrop, Ghana’s youth development efforts will need to focus not only on training but also on creating the economic environment in which young people can use those skills productively. Both advocates say creating opportunities for young people must therefore go beyond training programmes. While skills development remains critical, they argue that young people need access to markets, finance, mentorship, leadership platforms and decision-making spaces where they can translate their skills and ideas into tangible economic and social impact. Mr Appiah said young people from different parts of Ghana may operate in different sectors and come from different backgrounds, but their aspirations are largely similar. “We are all living in different contexts and building similar businesses, different businesses, but we all have the similar goal to be able to do more. We want to really be given the opportunity,” he said. He urged stakeholders to give young people “a seat at the table” so they can contribute to decisions affecting their future while also creating employment opportunities for others. For Ms Odonkor, her work through YIDA is similarly focused on using communication to amplify the contributions of young people and demonstrate how their skills can support community and national development. Together, their experiences point to a central challenge in Ghana’s youth development agenda: ensuring that investments in young people translate into real opportunities to work, build businesses, lead and create jobs. As International Youth Day 2026 draws attention to the different circumstances in which young people live, the advocates say the common aspiration remains clear – young people want the opportunity to learn, work, build, contribute and create better futures for themselves and others. For young entrepreneurs and professionals, the message is clear: training can provide the skills, but access to markets and opportunities to apply those skills could determine whether those investments produce lasting economic impact.

items.title: Stripe rachète OpenRouter pour piloter l’accès à plus de 400 modèles d’IA
items.description: Stripe a signé l’acquisition d’OpenRouter, une plateforme qui choisit un modèle d’IA selon le prix, la vitesse et la fiabilité. Les entreprises ne publient pas le montant; la presse américaine avance environ 7,5 milliards de dollars, chiffre qui reste attribué à des sources anonymes. Stripe étend son activité au-delà des paiements en ligne. Le groupe a annoncé le 19 août un accord pour acquérir OpenRouter, une plateforme qui donne accès à plus de 400 modèles provenant de plus de 80 fournisseurs. Les conditions financières officielles restent confidentielles et l’opération doit encore suivre les procédures habituelles avant sa finalisation. OpenRouter sert d’intermédiaire entre une application et plusieurs fournisseurs d’intelligence artificielle. Pour chaque demande, son système peut sélectionner un modèle en fonction de la complexité de la tâche, du prix, de la vitesse et de la disponibilité. Une entreprise évite ainsi de construire séparément des connexions avec des dizaines de services et peut modifier ses choix lorsque les tarifs ou les performances évoluent. Stripe présente l’achat comme le prolongement de ses outils de facturation à l’usage. Les modèles facturent souvent leur activité en jetons, unités qui représentent la quantité de texte ou de données traitée. Les deux sociétés veulent rapprocher la gestion de cette dépense du suivi des revenus. OpenRouter cite Nvidia, Zoom et Lovable parmi les entreprises utilisant déjà sa plateforme, sans publier dans l’annonce le volume de trafic ni le chiffre d’affaires associé à ces clients. Le prix rapporté donne une autre dimension au dossier. CNBC cite le New York Times, qui évalue la transaction à environ 7,5 milliards de dollars, dont 1,5 milliard destiné aux fondateurs d’OpenRouter. Stripe a refusé de commenter ce montant. CNBC rappelle qu’OpenRouter avait levé 113 millions de dollars moins de trois mois auparavant sur la base d’une valorisation proche de 1,3 milliard. Ces chiffres de presse ne doivent donc pas être présentés comme les termes confirmés du contrat. L’acquisition place Stripe dans une position sensible : le groupe pourrait intervenir à la fois dans la facturation et dans le choix de l’infrastructure d’IA utilisée par ses clients. L’utilité promise dépendra de la neutralité du routage, de la transparence des marges et de la continuité d’accès aux fournisseurs concurrents. Les entreprises devront aussi vérifier où transitent leurs données, quelles demandes sont conservées et comment les incidents sont répartis entre OpenRouter et le fournisseur final. Stripe ne précise pas encore le calendrier de clôture, le traitement futur de la marque OpenRouter ni les éventuels changements tarifaires. Les gains annoncés sur le coût et la performance restent à mesurer après l’intégration. La principale information confirmée demeure l’accord d’acquisition et l’ambition de gérer ensemble paiement, consommation de modèles et sélection technique. Cet article vous est proposé en collaboration avec Aïobi . Contact: team@aiobi.world L’article Stripe rachète OpenRouter pour piloter l’accès à plus de 400 modèles d’IA est apparu en premier sur Wakat Séra .

items.title: Siguiri érigée en région administrative et trois de ses sous-préfectures en préfectures : l’honorable Souleymane Koïta salue la décision
items.description: À la suite du quatrième Recensement général de la population et de l’habitation (RGPH-4), Siguiri compte désormais 1 718 147 habitants, faisant d’elle l’une des préfectures les plus peuplées du pays. Cette évolution traduit le poids démographique, économique et territorial de Siguiri. Dans un entretien téléphonique accordé à notre rédaction, l’honorable Souleymane Koïta s’est réjoui de l’érection de Siguiri en région administrative et de la transformation des sous-préfectures de Kintinian, Doko et Siguirini en préfectures. « Ce jeudi 19 août 2026, nous avons appris la décision du Chef de l’État, à travers un décret, portant érection de la préfecture de Siguiri en région administrative et des sous-préfectures de Kintinian, Doko et Siguirini en préfectures. Nous nous réjouissons de cette décision qui vient répondre à une attente portée par les populations de Siguiri, qui était d’ailleurs notre mot d’ordre lors des campagnes électorales passées. Nous, députés de Siguiri à l’Hémicycle, au nom des sages, des femmes et des jeunes, adressons nos remerciements à Monsieur le Président de la République, Son Excellence Mamadi Doumbouya, pour cette décision historique », a-t-il déclaré. Siguiri franchit ainsi une nouvelle étape de son histoire administrative. Nouhan Konaté, correspondant régional basé à Siguiri L’article Siguiri érigée en région administrative et trois de ses sous-préfectures en préfectures : l’honorable Souleymane Koïta salue la décision est apparu en premier sur Mediaguinee.com .

items.title: RDC : l’épidémie d’Ebola se propage rapidement, plus de 2500 morts
items.description: L'epidemie d'Ebola en Republique democratique du Congo a desormais depasse le seuil des 2 500 morts, alors que la maladie continue de se propager a un rythme qualifie d'« exponentiel » par les Nations unies. « L'epidemie d'Ebola connaît une croissance exponentielle », a declare le 21 août Julien Harneis, coordinateur principal des Nations unies d'Ebola, lors d'une visioconference depuis Bunia, dans le nord-est du pays. Selon lui, l'epidemie s'etend desormais sur une zone dont la surface est superieure a celle de la France, tandis que la reponse sanitaire progresse moins rapidement que la propagation du virus. « L'epidemie se propage plus rapidement et plus largement que la reponse a Ebola », at-il averti, soulignant que cette situation intervient dans une region confrontee a trois decennies de conflits armes et a d'importants besoins humanitaires. L'epidemie la plus importante de l'histoire du pays La RDC fait actuellement face a sa 17e epidemie d'Ebola . Fin juillet, elle est devenue la plus importante jamais enregistree dans le pays en nombre de cas, depassant le precedent record etabli lors de l'epidemie de 2018-2020. L'epidemie actuelle est provoquee par l'espece Bundibugyo du virus Ebola, pour laquelle aucun vaccin ni traitement homologue n'est actuellement disponible, selon les informations communiquees par l'ONU. Julien Harneis a egalement alerte sur la situation particulierement difficile des personnels de sante. Environ 160 agents de sante ont contracte la maladie, dont 43 sont morts. a la menace du virus s'ajoutent les violences visant les equipes chargees de la riposte. Plus de 266 attaques contre des personnels de sante ont ete enregistrees au cours des six derniers mois, selon le responsable onusien. Huit agents de sante ont ete tues. Des ambulances ont notamment ete caillassees ou incendiees et des etablissements de sante attaques. Ces violences sont alimentees par la peur, mais aussi par des rumeurs et des theories complotistes contestant la realite de l'epidemie. Une reponse sanitaire confrontee au manque de moyens Les organisations humanitaires font egalement face a d'importantes difficultes financieres. Les financements actuellement disponibles pour la reponse a Ebola devraient arriver a leur terme dans les prochaines semaines, a prevenu Julien Harneis, appelant a une mobilisation urgente de nouveaux fonds. Les reductions de l'aide internationale intervenues ces dernieres annees ont deja reduit les capacites d'intervention des organisations humanitaires. Le paiement des dizaines de milliers de personnes mobilisees dans la lutte contre l'epidemie constitue egalement un probleme. La suspension des vols commerciaux decidee par les autorites congolaises a perturbe les circuits d'approvisionnement en liquidites et affecte le fonctionnement des services bancaires. Face a l'extension rapide de l'epidemie, les Nations unies appellent ainsi a renforcer d'urgence les moyens humains, financiers et logistiques consacres a la riposte, alors que les equipes de sante doivent simultanement lutter contre le virus et faire face a un environnement securitaire particulierement difficile.

items.title: Ghana now spends less than 20% of revenue on servicing debt– Dr Ato Forson
items.description: The Minister for Finance, Dr Cassiel Ato Forson, says Ghana now spends less than 20% of its revenue on debt servicing, down from about 50% in the past. He said the previous debt-service burden left the country with fewer resources for schools, hospitals, roads and other critical infrastructure. “At its peak, we were spending about 50 per cent of our revenue on debt servicing. This meant less money for schools, hospitals, roads and other infrastructure. That was unsustainable,” Dr Forson said. “Today, I am proud to say that we have made considerable progress. We are now spending less than 20 per cent of our revenue on servicing debt.” He explained that the reduction has created more fiscal space for the Government to invest in public infrastructure and social services that directly improve the lives of Ghanaians. Dr Forson said the Government was also putting measures in place to prevent Ghana from returning to an unsustainable debt situation. “We are ensuring the fiscal rules we have instituted are enshrined in law, so that no matter which government is in office, these rules will be respected,” he stated. The Finance Minister made the remarks at the signing of an agreement between the Governments of Ghana and Belgium to restructure debt owed to Belgium’s export credit agency.

items.title: Des présidents et membres des CDS outillés à Oussouye
items.description: Pendant six jours, les présidents et membres des Comités de développement sanitaire (Cds) du district d'Oussouye ont été formés pour mieux maîtriser leurs missions, leurs responsabilités et les règles qui encadrent la gestion des structures de santé. OUSSOUYE – La gestion d’une structure sanitaire ne laisse plus de place à l’improvisation. Dans cette perspective, la gouvernance sanitaire veut changer de dimension. À Oussouye, l’International budget partnership (Ibp) Sénégal a mis l’accent sur la maîtrise des textes et règlements par les responsables des CDS, considérés comme des acteurs clés de la gouvernance sanitaire au niveau local. Ladite structure a initié une session de formation à l'endroit des responsables des CDS. L’objectif est clair : prévenir les erreurs, renforcer la transparence et éviter que de simples omissions dans l’application des textes ne se transforment en contentieux. « Nous exhortons les responsables des CDS à s’approprier les textes et à les respecter, car certains manquements peuvent avoir des conséquences judiciaires. Une bonne connaissance des règles est donc indispensable pour assurer correctement leurs missions », a déclaré Ibrahima Sidibé, représentant de l’IBP Sénégal. Ainsi, cette session de six jours intervient dans un contexte particulier. Les CDS récemment installés dans le district sanitaire d’Oussouye n’avaient pas encore bénéficié d’une formation spécifique sur leur fonctionnement et leurs responsabilités. Pour l'adjoint au médecin-chef de district, Dr Cheikh Ndiaye, cette session de renforcement de capacités doit permettre de faire émerger une gouvernance plus participative et plus efficace. « Cette formation vise à donner aux acteurs locaux les outils nécessaires pour comprendre le fonctionnement des CDS et améliorer la gestion sanitaire dans un esprit de transparence, de participation et d’efficacité », a-t-il expliqué. Au-delà de la formation, les organisateurs ambitionnent de rapprocher davantage collectivités territoriales, professionnels de santé et communautés. « Nous voulons que les CDS maîtrisent pleinement leur rôle et leurs responsabilités, tout en renforçant la collaboration entre les différents acteurs afin d’améliorer durablement la gouvernance sanitaire locale », a ajouté le Dr Ndiaye. L’autre enjeu est la mise en place d’un réseau des CDS, appelé à constituer un cadre de référence pour harmoniser la gestion technique et administrative des structures sanitaires. « La santé concerne directement les collectivités et les populations. Sa gouvernance doit donc être portée à un niveau élevé afin que les ressources du secteur profitent réellement aux communautés », a-t-il souligné, invitant les collectivités et les acteurs de la santé à mieux s’approprier les politiques publiques. La formation a concerné, dans un premier axe, les CDS d’Elinkine, Carabane, Cagnout et Cadjinolle. Le second axe a réuni ceux d’Oukout, Carounate, Loudia Wolof, Diakène Wolof, Diakène Diola et Youtou. Une étape importante pour faire de la maîtrise des règles et de la responsabilité des gestionnaires des leviers essentiels d’une meilleure gouvernance sanitaire à Oussouye. Kathafa B.H.M KANFOUDY (Correspondant)

items.title: Turkey issues ‘genocide’ warrant for Israel PM Netanyahu
items.description: Turkey has sought an international arrest warrant for Israel’s Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu accusing him of “genocide” linked to Israel’s interception of an aid flotilla for Gaza, the justice minister announced Friday. Turkey has become a virulent critic of Israel’s war in Gaza, sparked by the Hamas October 7, 2023 attacks on Israel. President Recep Tayyip Erdogan has frequently accused Netanyahu of “genocide”. Israel’s interception of the flotilla carrying some 430 activists in May sparked an international outcry. France, Italy and Australia have also launched judicial proceedings. Turkey’s Justice Minister Akin Gurlek said on X that his ministry had asked the interior ministry to issue interpol red notice alerts for Netanyahu and another Israeli, named as Afek Moskovitch. “As part of the judicial proceedings concerning the attack in international waters on the Flotilla activists (…) and in accordance with the arrest warrants issued on July 14, 2026, against Benjamin Netanyahu and Afek Moskovitch for ‘genocide,’ the ministry of justice has requested that the ministry of the interior issue red notices for their international arrest,” the minister stated. Netanyahu and Moskovitch are being prosecuted for “crimes against humanity, genocide, aggravated deprivation of liberty, ‘intentional assault and battery,’ torture, destruction of property, aggravated looting, and hijacking of transport vehicles,” the ministry said. About 50 vessels were in the Global Sumud Flotilla that left Turkey in May heading for the besieged Palestinian territory. The activists were detained in the Mediterranean by the Israeli military and then taken to an Israeli prison before being expelled. Israel’s far right National Security Minister Itamar Ben Gvir caused his own outcry by releasing a video showing himself taunting some of flotilla activists who were on their knees with their hands tied behind their backs. AFP The post Turkey issues ‘genocide’ warrant for Israel PM Netanyahu appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Meet Victoria Oluwakotanmi, former US navy officer crowned Miss Grand USA
items.description: Nigerian-American beauty queen Victoria Oluwakotanmi has stepped into the spotlight after becoming Miss Grand USA 2026. Oluwakotanmi, who finished as the first runner-up at the Miss Grand USA final held on August 10, assumed the crown on Friday after the organisation terminated the reign of the original winner, Mekayla Li. Her new title places her on an international stage, where she will represent the United States at the Miss Grand International pageant. However, Oluwakotanmi’s journey to the crown extends beyond pageantry, with a background spanning the US Navy, education and youth empowerment. Born and raised in San Antonio, Texas, Oluwakotanmi is the daughter of Nigerian immigrants and has spoken publicly about her Nigerian heritage and experience growing up in a Nigerian-American family. Long before she wore a pageant crown, Oluwakotanmi joined the United States Navy Reserve. She enlisted in March 2019 as a Logistics Specialist and has been associated with the Naval Operational Support Center San Antonio at Joint Base San Antonio-Fort Sam Houston. Her military service has formed an important part of her public identity as a young Black woman who served in the US armed forces. Oluwakotanmi began her pageant journey with the Miss Black San Antonio competition in February 2020. Her first competition came with little of the elaborate preparation often associated with beauty pageants. She later held the Miss Grand Illinois title and competed in Miss Texas USA as an at-large contestant. Away from pageantry and military service, Oluwakotanmi studied chemical engineering at Northwest Vista College while serving in the Navy. Education has also become an important part of her advocacy work. In 2018, Oluwakotanmi and her family founded the Oluwakotanmi Promise, a scholarship and mentorship programme established in honour of her late grandmother. According to Oluwakotanmi’s public accounts, her grandmother was denied the opportunity to attend college because of her gender. The initiative was created to support young people through education, mentorship and other opportunities. Oluwakotanmi has also shared updates about recipients of the programme, including members of its first cohort who graduated from high school in 2026. Her path to the Miss Grand USA crown, however, took an unexpected turn. Oluwakotanmi did not initially win the 2026 Miss Grand USA pageant. She finished as the first runner-up at the August 10 final, where Mekayla Li was crowned. However, after the Miss Grand USA organisation terminated Li’s reign and released her from the title and associated duties, Oluwakotanmi was elevated to Miss Grand USA 2026. items.title: Man City boss Maresca hit with Doku injury blow
items.description: Manchester City boss Enzo Maresca has suffered a blow on the eve of the Premier League season after Belgium winger Jeremy Doku was ruled out for several weeks. Doku will miss City’s Premier League opener against Bournemouth with a calf injury and is unlikely to return for up to three weeks. The 24-year-old suffered the problem during the first half of City’s 3-0 defeat against Arsenal in the Community Shield in Cardiff last weekend. Doku’s absence is a significant setback for former Chelsea boss Maresca as he starts his first season in charge at City after replacing Pep Guardiola in the close-season. “At the moment the only one out is Jeremy Doku,” Maresca told reporters on Friday. “Unfortunately in the last game, at half-time, he was complaining about a little bit of pain in his calf. “The idea with him was to play 45 minutes anyway, so the change was planned, but at the moment it looks like two or three weeks, no more than that.” After hosting Bournemouth, Maresca’s side travel to Crystal Palace, then face Coventry before the derby at Manchester United.
